plans.note: No liability or limitation heading appears in the outline; the only enumerated provisions exposed are 1.4 (access) and 5.4 (representatives). Scan the unexposed body under sec-p0001 for a limitation/damages clause before concluding a mutual cap must be added.

Missing-type rule: no indemnity heading surfaced. Expect to insert HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from the developed and hosted site, with our indemnity kept narrow to content we supply (Deerskin Products materials).

Presence check: no covenant or restrictive-covenant section is visible. Given this is an affiliate site development and hosting deal, verify the unexposed body does not restrict the Company's other channels or product sourcing.

Presence check: hosting agreements often make HDI the sole provider of site development/hosting. Nothing in the outline says so; confirm no exclusive-provider or sole-source language sits in the body under sec-p0001.
Direction check: no pricing or fees section is exposed, so no MFN language is visible. If a most-favoured-terms clause exists in the unexposed body, confirm it runs in our favour, not HDI's.

Presence check: 5.4 concerns appointed representatives and is the most likely magnet for personnel covenants; otherwise no non-solicit appears. If one exists, seek 12 months and a general-advertising carve-out.

'Termination Date' is a defined term, so termination mechanics exist in the body even though no heading is exposed. Locate them under sec-p0001 and test for a Company right to terminate on notice without penalty and no mid-term HDI walk-away.

Term/renewal language should accompany the defined 'Termination Date' in the unexposed body under sec-p0001; check for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any uncapped renewal price escalation.
Boilerplate typically sits in the closing article immediately before the signature block (sec-p0072); confirm governing law is NY/DE/CA/E&W with courts rather than arbitration.

Assignment is standard back-end boilerplate; look just before the execution block. Because HDI and the Company are related entities, watch for HDI termination or consent rights triggered by a change of control of the Company.

Direction check: 1.4 grants the Company access to HDI systems/materials and is the closest exposed hook. Confirm ownership of the developed site, Deerskin Products content and customer data vests in us, with no assignment of our IP or data to HDI.
Section 1.4 (access to HDI resources) is the likely licence/access grant; test scope for affiliates and contractors and remove any revocable-at-will or unilaterally suspendable access right.

No audit or records heading is exposed; 5.4's representative mechanism is the nearest governance hook. If HDI has audit rights over our usage, require notice, limited frequency, off-site review and HDI's cost.

Direction check: no fees, service-level or remedies section is exposed, so no liquidated damages are visible. Confirm the unexposed body imposes no penalty or stipulated damages on the Company; service credits running to us are acceptable.

No warranty or service-level heading surfaced. Check the body under sec-p0001 for an HDI performance warranty on the developed site and hosting uptime; if absent, add one with a meaningful duration and repair/re-perform remedy.

Missing-type rule: no insurance provision appears anywhere in the outline. HDI hosts our site and handles customer data, so standard coverage (including cyber/tech E&O) should be added, likely alongside the indemnity.
Presence check: no fees, minimum volume or take-or-pay language is exposed. Verify the unexposed commercial terms do not commit the Company to minimum hosting or development spend without an exit.

Missing-type rule: 'Termination Date' is defined but no transition or data-return provision is exposed. Add wind-down assistance and return/deletion of our site content and customer data, tying it to the access rights in 1.4.
